questions.question: Kinetic energy is the energy an object has because of its:
In E_k = ½mv², doubling the mass at the same speed:
options: Doubles the kinetic energy — mass enters the formula plainly, once

questions.question: A car doing 20 m/s east and an identical car doing 20 m/s west have:
options: Identical kinetic energies — squaring the velocity erases direction
Energies differing by the sign of v

questions.question: Kinetic energy can never be negative because:
options: Energy is a vector pointing forward
Mass is positive and v² cannot go below zero — rest, at zero, is the floor

subtopics.title: Pricing the Motion — a Tonne at Twenty

questions.question: For the 1 000 kg car at 20 m/s, the kinetic energy is:
A learner who forgets to square the 20 gets 10 000 J — an answer:
When the car stops normally, its 200 000 J are:
options: Converted to heat in the brakes
Stored in the tyres as pressure

questions.question: A speed given as 72 km/h must be handled as:
options: Divide by 3,6 after all other steps
Divide by 3,6 to get 20 m/s BEFORE squaring

subtopics.title: The Square — Why Doubling Speed Quadruples the Danger

questions.question: Doubling the car's speed from 20 to 40 m/s changes its kinetic energy from 200 000 J to:
Tripling a speed multiplies the kinetic energy by:
For the same braking force, four times the kinetic energy means roughly:
Going from 100 to 120 km/h adds MORE energy than going from 0 to 60 km/h because:
options: Highways are longer than town roads
Energy grows with the square of speed, so the top of the range is where energy piles up
Engines work harder in top gear
The comparison is a trick — it adds less

subtopics.title: The Full Method, the Classic Traps, and Where This Leads

questions.question: The recommended defence against the forgotten square is:
options: Writing v² as its own line before assembling the formula
Using km/h so the numbers are bigger

questions.question: Squaring 72 km/h instead of 20 m/s inflates the answer by a factor of about:
Leaving out the half in ½mv²:
An object moving in the NEGATIVE direction of the frame has kinetic energy that is:
options: Positive — the square destroys the sign

questions.question: In the wallet picture, stopping an object means:
options: The cash is saved for the next trip
Every cent of the motion-cash is spent on whatever does the stopping
The wallet is refilled by the brakes

questions.question: The two dials of the price list behave as:
options: Mass plain (twice the load, twice the cash); speed squared (twice the pace, four times the cash)

questions.question: A full taxi versus the same taxi empty, at the same speed, carries:
options: The same energy — speed is all that matters
About double the kinetic energy, from the mass dial
Four times the energy, from the square
Less energy, because it moves lower

questions.question: 'Standing still is an empty wallet' means:
options: Objects at rest have negative energy
Stationary objects have potential energy only in motion problems
An object at rest has zero kinetic energy

questions.question: The counting order used in the lesson is:
options: Half the speed, then square the mass
Multiply mass by speed, then halve
Square the speed first (20 × 20 = 400), then half the mass (500), then multiply
Add mass and speed, then square

questions.question: The 200 000 J was given a picture: it equals the 2 kg brick lifted:
options: One hundred metres up a tower

questions.question: Crumple zones are designed to fold in a crash because:
options: Folded metal is cheaper to repair
Folding metal spends the car's huge kinetic energy over distance — the least bad way to spend a fortune fast
Folding stores the energy for later

questions.question: The 'wallet twenty times too thin' error comes from:
options: Skipping the square — multiplying by a plain 20 instead of 400

questions.question: The 'quadratic surcharge' names the fact that:
options: Kinetic energy grows with the square of the speed
Mass and speed both double together
Brakes wear out four times faster

questions.question: At 40 m/s the 1 000 kg car carries:
options: 800 000 J — four times its energy at 20 m/s

questions.question: 'A collision at 80 is four collisions at 40 happening at once' because:
options: Doubling speed quadruples the energy the crash must absorb

questions.question: When two speeds are compared for danger, the lesson says compare:
options: Their squares — because that is how the road compares them
